verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Both inequalities are present, in coefficient form and with the paper's abstract multiplication bound instantiated. (i) The 𝒥₂ bound is `regularInverseJet_bound_on_order`: for data whose radial coefficients vanish below degree k (= the paper's b) each weighted jet obeys |𝒥₂f|ₙₘ ≤ (80/((k+1)(k+2)))·F·weight, which is the paper's operator inequality in the norm (B.4) because the Lean norm is the supremum of |jet|/weight (`axis_abs_jet_le` and `axis_norm_le_of_jet_bound`, AxisResolvent.lean:306 and :312); the Lean weight (AxisWeightEstimates.lean:28) is literally the (B.4) weight 20^{-n}ρ^{-m}m!C(n+m,m)/((n+1)²(m+1)²) with ε = ρ. (ii) `naturalOperator_pow_bound` is the second inequality for T = (1/2)𝒥₂M_χ, in the same shape K^k/(k!(k+1)!), with K = 2560‖χ‖ = 40·(64‖χ‖): the paper's M_χ (any bound for multiplication by χ on B_ρ) is instantiated by the Lean algebra constant 64‖χ‖ of `jetProduct_bound`. The constant is therefore the paper's with an explicit M_χ, not a weaker one.
